stops.note: literally '100,000', a reference to the vast numbers of insects that produce the resin
the vernacular form carried the word into everyday speech
settled as the everyday North Indian word for the resin
traders adopted the Hindi word for the traded commodity
stops.meaning: resin used in varnish and dye

stops.note: entered English via Persian-Indian trade for the insect resin used in varnish
stops.meaning: a resinous secretion used for varnish and dye

current_meaning: A resinous secretion of the lac insect, used to make shellac, varnish, and dye.
